details: Bitcoin, after experiencing a volatile week and dipping below $60,000, has seen a recovery, trading around $63,500 by Saturday. This rebound is attributed to renewed market risk appetite following signals of de-escalation in the Iran conflict and the successful 20% debut surge of SpaceX's Initial Public Offering (IPO) on Nasdaq. SpaceX's IPO also indirectly increased Bitcoin exposure in public markets due to the company's significant BTC holdings.
title: Bitcoin Recovers as SpaceX IPO, Iran De-escalation Boost Risk Appetite

details: Global markets are closely watching central bank actions amid persistent inflation concerns. The European Central Bank (ECB) recently raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, its first hike since 2023, citing inflationary pressures. In the U.S., despite hopes for a rate cut, a hotter-than-expected Producer Price Index (PPI) and strong consumer inflation expectations data are reinforcing fears of a hawkish Federal Reserve, which is expected to keep rates paused at its upcoming meeting. The Bank of Japan is also anticipated to hike rates.
title: Central Banks Signal Tightening as ECB Hikes, Fed Outlook Remains Cautious

details: MicroStrategy (now Strategy Inc.), a major corporate holder of Bitcoin, disclosed the sale of 32 Bitcoins for approximately $2.5 million between May 26 and May 31. This marks the company's first Bitcoin sale since 2022, challenging its long-held "never sell" stance and raising questions among traders about its unwavering accumulation strategy. The small sale, while financially minor, was seen as a significant behavioral shift, impacting sentiment across the broader crypto market.
title: MicroStrategy's Bitcoin Sale Sparks Debate on Corporate Crypto Strategy

details: A significant trend in financial markets shows speculative capital increasingly favoring artificial intelligence (AI) and tech stocks over cryptocurrencies. Reports indicate that tech shares, particularly those connected to AI, are driving a majority of earnings growth and market returns in 2026. This shift suggests that investors seeking high-growth opportunities are reallocating funds to the perceived "hotter markets" of AI, potentially leading to underperformance in broader cryptocurrency markets.
title: AI Stocks Outperform, Drawing Speculative Capital Away from Crypto
